name: Supplying what is understood (taqdīr)
definition: Assuming a word, a vowel or a governor that is not pronounced but is needed to explain the iʿrāb: the vowel 'assumed' on a word ending in alif, the hidden subject of a verb, the governor of an adverbial phrase.
body: Taqdīr works at two levels. On the ending of a word it gives the assumed iʿrāb (iʿrāb taqdīrī): in jāʾa al-fatā the ḍamma cannot be pronounced on the final alif and is said to be muqaddara. In the sentence it supplies what is understood: in zaydun fī al-dāri the phrase fī al-dāri hangs on an unspoken word such as 'is settled' (kāʾinun or istaqarra), and a verb has a hidden pronoun as its subject when none is expressed.
The commentaries are full of it ('its taqdīr is…', 'by the taqdīr of…'), and its overuse was one of Ibn Maḍāʾ's charges against the grammarians.

examples.text: The young man came: al-fatā is in rafʿ by an assumed ḍamma (muqaddara) on the alif.
Zayd is in the house: the predicate is the phrase fī al-dāri, attached to an understood word ('is settled').
